title: Block: Fast and Slow Pointers
oneLiner: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place with a slow pointer that writes and a fast pointer that reads.
keyTakeaway: One pointer reads every element, the other marks where the next keeper goes. Compare against what you last kept, not against the previous element you read.
explanation:
nums is sorted. Move its distinct values to the front, in order, without a second array, and return that front part. [0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2] gives [0, 1, 2].

slow is the index of the last value kept, starting at 0. fast walks from 1 to the end. When nums[fast] differs from nums[slow], move slow forward one and copy nums[fast] there. The first slow + 1 elements are the answer. Move Zeroes, Remove Element and partition steps are this block with a different keep test.

starterCode.python:
def dedupe_sorted(nums):
    # 1. If the array is empty, return it.
    # 2. Keep a slow pointer at the last unique value written, starting at index 0.
    # 3. Move a fast pointer from index 1 to the end.
    # 4. When nums[fast] differs from nums[slow], move slow forward and copy the value there.
    # 5. Return the first slow + 1 elements.
    return nums

gotchas: Starting slow at -1 or fast at 0, which compares an element with itself or reads out of range.
Returning slow elements instead of slow + 1.

complexity.note: The fast pointer reads each element once and the writes happen in place. Returning the front part as a new array copies up to n values.
